Resolves #19040

A second root of a canvas-drawing SharedWorker app, opened with no opener, terminates the first root's renderer. That had been measured three times and never once from a spec in this repository — `#18376`'s body records what that cost: *"The 2026-09-05 probe was written outside the tree and is gone."* This commits the witness, and it lands inside `RUN_PATHS` rather than in the GPU-excluded workstation directory, so CI actually executes it.

Evidence: L4 (local real Chromium, `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, three arms plus two mutation arms at `4eb40a7ab9`) → L4 required (every AC on #19040 is a spec-shape or run-shape criterion, and the red arm can only be certified by running it). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: no — the `test.fail()` inversion is a convention choice worth a reviewer's judgement, not a mechanical change.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — lives in `e2e/core`, no Brain root, no GPU | `test/playwright/e2e/core/NoOpenerRootRendererKill.spec.mjs`; `e2eCiSelection.mjs`'s `RUN_PATHS` contains `test/playwright/e2e/core`, verified by importing the module rather than reading the array by eye |
| AC-2 — three arms, controls pass, red arm `test.fail()`, suite green | outside-CI: `npx playwright test core/NoOpenerRootRendererKill -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1` → `3 passed (22.2s)` |
| AC-3 — mutation-checked both ways | outside-CI: both runs below, under **Test Evidence** |
| AC-4 — docblock names the witness and states the limit | `NoOpenerRootRendererKill.spec.mjs:3-24` — the frame-sink mechanism, `apps/portal` over the workstation app, and the paragraph beginning *"The two controls are load-bearing, and the honest limit is why"* |
| AC-5 — `0 new` fixed sleeps | `node buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` → `OK — 3 unaccounted site(s) baselined, 0 new, 0 stale`; the three settle waits carry `wall-clock-under-test:` |

## Deltas from ticket

**One, and it is a change to the parent's wording rather than to this leaf.** `#18376`'s AC-1 specifies *"two full Workstation roots"*. Taken literally that produces a spec no CI job runs: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation` is a declared GPU exclusion in `e2eCiSelection.mjs`, and every spec there is a Neural Link spec that `testIgnore` deselects without `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` — the `Skipped: 0` failure mode that file's own docblock warns about. `apps/portal` is the affected configuration too (`useCanvasWorker: true`, `useSharedWorkers: true`, four canvas consumers) and carries no animated offscreen work. The app-agnostic AC-1 wording is proposed to the parent's author at [issuecomment-5761503618](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18376#issuecomment-5761503618); this PR does not depend on that proposal being accepted.

The Workstation arm is untouched and stays `#18376`'s AC-3.

## Test Evidence

Outside CI, all at `4eb40a7ab9`, one worker, serially:

```
3 passed (22.2s)
```

Mutation arms, because `test.fail()` is satisfied by **any** failure and would otherwise keep reporting success after `apps/portal` stopped booting at all:

| mutation | result | what it rules out |
|---|---|---|
| `test.fail()` removed | `1 failed, 2 passed` — and it fails at `root A must survive a second root that owns its own renderer process`, the named assertion, not at a timeout in flight | that the arm is green for a reason unrelated to the crash |
| launch swapped `context.newPage()` → `window.open` | `Expected to fail, but passed` — `1 failed, 2 passed` | that the arm witnesses "a second root exists" rather than the process boundary |

The second is the load-bearing one: only the launch path changed between them.

The two controls are what bound `test.fail()`'s looseness, and the docblock says so rather than implying the arm is airtight on its own.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-21T14:03:40Z

## The first Post-Merge Validation item is discharged **before** merge

I wrote it as post-merge because a hosted runner is a different renderer-process budget from this machine, and a crash is exactly the class of behaviour that can differ. It does not: all three arms executed on GitHub's Ubuntu runner in `e2e-engine (1/2)`, [run 35608853012](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35608853012), at `4eb40a7ab9`.

```
✓  21  … › control: root A alone survives the window the red arm dies in          (10.3s)
✓  22  … › control: a root that shares root A's renderer process does not kill it  (11.9s)
✘  23  … › a root with no opener kills root A                                      (3.5s)

119 passed (4.1m)
```

The `✘` on arm 23 is the `test.fail()` arm failing as declared — the suite reports `119 passed` and the shard is green. The shard also proves the spec was **selected**, not merely not-excluded, which is the distinction `e2eCiSelection.mjs`'s docblock exists to make.

Two readings worth keeping:

- **The kill is not local to my machine.** It reproduces on a hosted headless runner, which is the environment every future contributor's PR runs in.
- **It lands faster there:** 3.5 s against the 8 s settle window this spec allows. The measured timing in `#18376` — the kill ~0.4 s into root B's boot, root A gone within 4.7 s — holds on CI, so the settle window has roughly twice the headroom it needs rather than being tuned to one machine.

The second validation item stands as written: when `#18376`'s fix lands, this file reds with *"Expected to fail, but passed"*, and the fix's PR deletes line 115. That red is the signal.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code
